title: Prime Agents get an automatic upkeep rebate for holding each other's tokens, creating a structural incentive to cross-hold
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.3.2.2.1.1 states the entitlement and then explains why the Parameters section is empty: "Every Prime Agent is entitled to the Upkeep Rebate Primitive for tokens of other Prime Agents that they hold. Because this right automatically applies, there are no parameters."

Two operational facts complete the mechanism. A.6.1.1.2.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.1: "Grove keeps all tokens of other Agents it holds in its SubProxy account." A.6.1.1.2.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.2: "When paying Ecosystem Upkeep fees, Grove deducts the rebate from the fees it pays."

The economic effect is a **cross-holding subsidy between Agents**. An Agent that holds other Agents' tokens pays less into ecosystem upkeep, so mutual shareholding is cheaper than independence. That pushes the Agent layer toward being a mutually invested federation rather than a set of unrelated competitors — Agents have a direct financial reason to want each other to succeed, because another Agent's token appreciating both grows their treasury and enlarges their rebate.

Mandating custody in the **SubProxy** rather than a Foundation or Labs multisig is what makes the rebate self-verifying: the holdings are at a known onchain address under governance control, so the rebate base can be checked by anyone rather than asserted by the Agent.

The deduction-at-source design (netting rather than claiming) removes a payment cycle but also means the Agent computes its own bill. That is exactly why the review step in A.6.1.1.2.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.3 exists.
description: The entitlement 'automatically applies' and therefore has no parameters at all; Grove deducts the rebate directly from the Ecosystem Upkeep Fee it owes rather than claiming it separately.
